paper.central_claim: Skills-Coach is an automated framework (task generation, Training-Free-GRPO optimization of skill instructions and code, comparative execution, traceable evaluation with retain/discard decisions) that self-evolves LLM-agent skills without human intervention, raising skill capability on the 48-skill Skill-X benchmark (avg score 0.378 -> 0.84, pass rate 33.59% -> 88.02%).
paper.title: Skills-Coach: A Self-Evolving Skill Optimizer via Training-Free GRPO

gap.author_gap: The skill ecosystem has abundant volume but fragmented coverage; individually authored skills handle localized cases and leave functional gaps.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible practitioner problem but asserted with generic citations; the method does not expand coverage, it raises scores of existing skills on tasks generated from their own specification. The residue 'skills perform poorly on boundary tasks' is evidenced only by the authors' own low baseline scores.
gap.lineage: Prompt optimization (OPRO/TextGrad/DSPy-style, cited as method sources) and Training-Free GRPO -> reflection/self-refine -> skill ecosystems (Anthropic Agent Skills, Clawhub).
gap.closest_adjacent: Skill-evolution systems such as skill-creator and self-evolving-skill appear only as benchmark items being optimized; no skill-optimization baseline is compared.
gap.residue: Automated improvement of third-party skills without human intervention.
gap.stakes: Not quantified; 56,000 skills exist on Clawhub.
gap.remaining_gap: Real downstream agent success with optimized skills, versus alternative optimizers, ecosystem consistency, cost.
gap.unresolved: Whether score gains reflect utility or rubric conformity.

rs_pattern.reason: Opus sides with son55. There is no ground-truth supervision per skill; the pipeline manufactures it (generated train/test tasks, generated validation criteria, LLM judging, group-relative variant scores) and adapts the artifact on that signal. Sub null: C08/C26 assume a trained model as the adapted object. sol's adapt_via_conditioning (the optimised skill conditions a later agent) is generic to every skill paper, and heterogeneous_decomposition (instruction-only vs code-inclusive paths) describes a routing detail, not the paper's operation.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Signature steps executed: missing supervision identified, tasks/criteria/scores derived from the model and the artifact specification, artifact adapted on that signal. Sub-card tactics C08 (generate synthetic instances then a quality gate then retrain) and C26 (comparative/scalar rewards from a non-human judge optimized contrastively) are partially analogous but the adapted object is a text/code artifact, not a trained model, so no sub-card is assigned.
matches.success_failure_checks: Reviewer expectations: ablation vs simple baseline unmet; side-by-side on actual downstream objective unmet (proxy documentation scores); generalization beyond one model family unmet; cost of loop unmet.
matches.reason: Parent fits the operation; fit is partial because the manufactured signal is also the evaluation metric.

Instruction text varied (3 variants/epoch), scored on a small generated set, best kept; no search-vs-simpler-selector ablation, cost not reported, fitness is a generated rubric (S2 unmet).

claims.text: Skills-Coach significantly improves skill capability on Skill-X.
claims.setting: 48 public skills (29 instruction-only, 19 code-inclusive); claude-sonnet-4-6; 3 epochs; real mode

claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported: pipeline-rewritten skills score higher than originals on the pipeline's own generated tasks and rubric.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: on 48 public skills the pipeline's rewritten skill files score higher than the originals on 8 pipeline-generated test tasks per skill under the pipeline's own rubric (execution-based checks for 19 code skills, LLM-judged documentation dimensions for 29 instruction skills). Not shown: improved real agent task success, retained reuse, advantage over simple rewrites or other optimizers, or any cost. Held at task because evaluation tasks, rubric and retention decision come from the same pipeline.
unresolved: Metric validity (Goodhart), alternative optimizer baselines, downstream use, ecosystem consistency, cost, variance.

G.reason: Opus sides with son55. 'Abundant volume but fragmented coverage' is asserted with generic citations, and the method (optimising one skill against tasks derived from its own documentation) does not address ecosystem coverage. The nearest neighbours — prompt/code optimisers (TextGrad, DSPy, APO, cited as method sources) and existing skill-improvement skills (skill-creator, self-evolving-skill, which sit inside Skill-X itself) — are not positioned. Between 0 and 2.

M.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. A concrete pipeline (generated tasks, grouped variant selection, rule/LLM/auto-fix code optimisation, paired comparison, retain/discard) with execution evidence for code skills. 'Training-free GRPO' reduces to best-of-3 selection, the optimisation signal is the evaluation rubric, and the rule-driven optimiser inserts rubric features (opus:O04).

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Epochs, group size, task counts, isolation and modes are specified; the retention rule, persistence/versioning, rollback, ecosystem-consistency handling and later reading by an agent are missing.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked, with an Opus addition (shared omission, no rating change). Code-skill checks are execution-based but shallow (file existence, keywords, regex); 29 of 48 skills are LLM-scored on documentation-form criteria an optimiser can satisfy by restructuring; tasks and criteria come from the optimising pipeline. The reported numbers also do not fit the stated protocol (opus:O01, opus:O02, opus:O05).

E.causality.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. Only original vs optimised; no ablation of GRPO selection, auto-fix or task generation, and no one-shot rewrite, alternative optimiser or equal-budget baseline, so gains cannot be separated from rubric-conforming rewriting (opus:O04).

E.holdout.reason: Opus sides with son55. Train and test tasks are separate but come from the same generator and specification; the retain-or-discard decision is made on the test comparison that is reported (son55:E017, son55:E018), and Table 2 shows no regression across 48 skills (opus:O03); no external task or downstream agent run exists. sol's 2 relied on variant selection using the training set, which does not cover the final retention.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 tier 1): per-skill rows and the no-gain cases are reported; single run, no intervals or variance, means over ~8 tasks per skill.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with sol. Epochs, group size, task counts, fix rounds and model are settings, not cost (r12a UI-Mem, r13b PsychAgent precedent); the 'hours to minutes' and 'thousands to dozens' claims are unmeasured, and no tokens, calls, time or dollars are given.
